supports.ask: Why is the bending moment zero at a simple support?

loads.label: 5 kN/m
loads.ask: What is the maximum bending moment for a uniformly distributed load?

explain.say: Stand in the middle of a plank across a stream and it sags most right under your feet. That bending is measured by the bending moment, force times distance, in kilonewton metres. A bending moment diagram shows it at every point. Here is an eight metre beam with five kilonewtons per metre spread along it.

loads.label: 5 kN/m
loads.ask: What is the maximum bending moment for a uniformly distributed load?

explain.say: Look at the curve below the beam. It is zero at both ends, because a pin and a roller cannot resist turning, and it rises to a peak in the middle. For a spread load the shape is a parabola, a smooth arch. Where is the beam working hardest?

loads.label: 5 kN/m
loads.ask: What is the maximum bending moment for a uniformly distributed load?

explain.say: In the middle. The peak is w L squared over eight: five times sixty four, over eight, which is forty kilonewton metres. Positive here means sagging, a smile shape, with the bottom stretched and the top squashed. Which face of the beam is in tension?

loads.label: 5 kN/m
loads.ask: What is the maximum bending moment for a uniformly distributed load?

explain.say: The bottom face! Now gather the same forty kilonewtons into one point at midspan. The diagram becomes a triangle with a peak of P L over four: forty times eight over four, eighty kilonewton metres. Twice as much! Concentrated loads are much harsher than spread ones.

explain.say: That is why heavy machines sit on wide spreader plates. Great job. Remember the pattern: point loads give straight lines with corners, spread loads give curves, and the area under the shear diagram adds up to the moment. Exam tip: w L squared over eight is worth knowing by heart.

faq.a: A bending moment is the turning effect of the forces on one side of a section, force times distance, in kilonewton metres. It is what makes a beam curve.

faq.q: Why is the bending moment zero at a simple support?
faq.a: A pin or a roller lets the beam rotate freely, so it cannot hold any turning effect. The moment there is zero.
asks: Why is moment zero at a pin?

faq.q: What is the maximum bending moment for a uniformly distributed load?
faq.a: For a simply supported beam it is w L squared over eight, at midspan. Five kilonewtons per metre over eight metres gives 40 kilonewton metres.

faq.q: What is the difference between sagging and hogging?
faq.a: Sagging bends the beam into a smile, with tension at the bottom. Hogging bends it into a frown, with tension at the top, as over a support or in a cantilever.

faq.q: How is the bending moment diagram related to the shear force diagram?
faq.a: The moment at a point equals the area under the shear diagram up to that point, and the slope of the moment curve equals the shear.

facts: For a simply supported beam, a central point load P gives a maximum moment PL/4 and a uniform load w gives wL²/8.
Bending stress follows σ = My/I, so the fibres farthest from the neutral axis carry the most stress.

quiz.say: A six metre simply supported beam carries 10 kilonewtons per metre. What is the maximum bending moment?
quiz.show: A 6 m simply supported beam carries 10 kN/m. Maximum bending moment?
quiz.why: w L squared over eight: 10 × 36 / 8 = 45 kilonewton metres.

wrong.1: That divides by four instead of eight.
wrong.2: Thirty kilonewtons is the support reaction, not a moment.

quiz.say: Under a uniform load, the bending moment diagram of a simply supported beam is a…
quiz.show: Under a uniform load, the bending moment diagram of a simply supported beam is a…
quiz.why: A uniform load makes the shear slope linearly, so the moment is a parabola.

wrong.0: A triangle comes from a single point load.
wrong.2: A constant moment needs equal end couples, not a spread load.
